programme.title: Sky's The Limit
programme.desc: A documentary exploring the muralist movement: the art of painting over breathtaking heights. Windowless gable walls were graffiti painters’ early targets, particularly in urban areas under renovation, and since 2012, monumental graffiti is in full rebirth especially in Paris’ 13th arrondissement. Through a design thought as a décor, obliterating the blandness of the walls, artists skillfully revive these soulless surfaces.

programme.title: The Rivers
programme.desc: Mai Hua, French-Vietnamese single mom with two children, brings back her dying grandmother to France. As she miraculously recovers, questions are raised on the family's origins and a spell on women in the family. An intimate archeology of female lineage and universal quest for one's own truth.

programme.title: Dances with the Wind
programme.desc: ‘Fury Dance’ is a story about a Korean protest dancer, Sam-hun Lee. He fought for the democratization of South Korea in the ‘80’s through dance, while giving up his own dream to become a ballerino. The film takes the viewer through prominent events in South Korean history, as Sam-hun dances to soothe the souls of victims who were killed by the Korean national violence during the past 30 years. During the 1980 Gwangju Massacre however, Sam-hun developed a panic disorder. So he crosses through the Eurasian rail with difficulty when invited to attend a festival to dance in France. Through his journey, he attempts to overcome his claustrophobic fears in France, revisits his lost dream of becoming a ballerino in Russia, and dances for the Holocaust victims in Poland. Documented for 15 years, this film is dedicated to those who lost their noble lives while fighting for freedom against the unjust political power.

programme.title: Nothing Good Ever Happens
programme.desc: Neil who is a painter and graphic designer, on a morning just like any other morning his girlfriend Amanda leaves him and moves out of their house (don't worry, it's a rental.) That morning Neil tries to cope as best he knows how, but in a strange turn of events he ends up shooting back a glass of bleach. He wakes up to suicide watch and court appointed therapy as well as the empty void Amanda left. Now Neil has to decide what he can do to feel better about himself. Should he get Amanda back? Make his old friends like him again? Confront his estranged father? Eat a ton of Chinese food? Or maybe he should just finish his latest goddamned painting.

programme.title: Gumshoe
programme.desc: When hopeless New Orleans private eye Biff Basham is hired by a seductive nightclub singer to pay off a blackmailer, he thinks his money worries are over. But when his client's husband is murdered, he is plunged into a dangerous world of organized crime and espionage in this zany comedy. Can Biff unmask the killer before he becomes the next victim?

programme.title: Frank & Fearless
programme.desc: An aging reprobate, a rural boy, a large dog and an orphaned baby rhino set out to stop the rhino slaughter. Their quest buffets them between high comedy and searing tragedy, until they end up an inspiration and a conscience to a world in need of heroes.

programme.title: 1st Bite
programme.desc: Set on a tropical island in Thailand, the strange plight of a beleaguered chef who, while romancing a mysterious woman, discovers the diabolical Zen of cooking. Following a near death escape, he returns to Montreal and falls hard for the woman of his life who unfortunately craves only his cooking but not his loving. Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: A Raunchy Christmas Story
programme.desc: A group of pre millennials arrange a secluded Christmas party to put the romance back into a friend's life. Unbeknownst to them an investigative journalist and a soviet spy are among the guests.

programme.title: Cabin of Errors
programme.desc: When Peter and Nancy split up, their friends plot to bring them back together during a trip to a cabin. But things go hilariously wrong when Peter comes to the cabin with other intentions. A modern day romantic comedy farce.

programme.title: Úrsula Corberó y Chino Darin son puro fuego I Brujas de Zugarramurdi I Ministerio de brujas
programme.desc: Bienvenidas al Ministerio de Brujas, donde cada martes a las 20h en Canal Barro, se enciende la hoguera y se queman verdades incómodas. En este episodio, Carlos inauguró la nueva Subsecretaría de Misterios, trayendo algunas de las historias más oscuras y fascinantes de España: Las brujas de Zugarramurdi. La Inquisición y sus castigos. Y esos misterios que siguen latiendo entre cuevas, sombras y supersticiones. Como siempre, en la hoguera ardieron muchas cosas: – Reglas imposibles. – Gente manipuladora que tensa la cuerda. – Vampiros energéticos y demás criaturas emocionales. Pero el clímax llegó cuando las brujas leyeron las cartas astrales de Úrsula Corberó y Chino Darín en vivo. Él, con gen de líder pero alma aniñada y sexy. Ella, fuego puro, control y magnetismo. Juntos, una conexión casi kármica y familiar. Además, se destacó en el Departamento de Archivos Clasificados a una nueva bruja ilustre: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, la voz que hechiza desde el feminismo y la palabra. Y para cerrar con placer y picardía, en la Secretaría de Venus en Tanga, hubo tarot erótico: deseo, destino y mucha, mucha energía ardiente. Ministerio de Brujas: el único ministerio donde el fuego limpia, el deseo guía y la magia es ley. Todos los martes a las 20h (España) en @CanalBarro .

programme.title: Claudia Luchetti abre portales en vivo | La decodificadora más famosa en Ministerio de Brujas
programme.desc: En este nuevo capítulo del Ministerio de Brujas, las ministras del zodiaco reciben a una invitada especial: Claudia Luchetti, la decodificadora más famosa de Argentina, una mujer que camina entre la neurociencia, la Kábbalah y la energía invisible. Coach, conferencista y bruja de luz, Claudia nos cuenta cómo llega a ser bruja, qué siente cuando baja información, y cuáles fueron los casos más paranormales que vivió acompañando a otros en su transformación. Además, en esta edición: El Protocolo de la Hoguera: lo que decidimos quemar —desde los machirulos hasta los taladros del vecino. Secretaría de Venus en Tanga: exploramos la energía erótica de Tauro, los placeres mundanos, los aromas, las texturas y los sentidos. Cinematografía Zodiazal: nuevas películas bajo la lupa astrológica. Boletín de Movimientos Planetarios: con ChongaZen desentrañando el clima cósmico. Archivos Clasificados de Brujas: hoy, la artista Tracey Emin, la mujer que transformó su cama en arte y su dolor en revolución. Y como siempre, los Sindicatos Zodiacales elevan sus reclamos: Acuario: “Podridos de que nos digan fríos.” Cáncer: “¿Todo tenemos que sentir?” Libra: “¡Basta de falsedad!” Capricornio (sindicato de Claudia): “Queremos reconocimiento celestial por exceso de responsabilidad terrenal.” El Ministerio de Brujas no explica. Encanta. Entre astros, carcajadas y conjuros, abrimos portales donde otros archivan silencios. Todos los martes 20:00 (España) / 15:00 (Argentina) En YouTube y Kick de @canalbarro #MinisterioDeBrujas #ClaudiaLuchetti #Decodificacion #Astrologia #Brujas #Kabbalah #Neurociencia #Espiritualidad #Streaming #BarroTV #Astros #FeminismoMagico #TraceyEmin

programme.title: Ministerio de Brujas: el primer gobierno astral de la historia #astrologia #esoterismo #tarot
programme.desc: Bienvenidas, bienvenidos y bienvenides al Ministerio de Brujas, el nuevo programa del Canal Barro donde la intuición, el arte y la magia se sientan a la misma mesa. Este primer episodio es un aquelarre de verdad: fuego, deseo, política, feminismo y mucho humor. Las ministras @chongazen, @marianaenvozalta y @zakurapill abren las puertas del ministerio con un comunicado oficial: “El Ministerio de Brujas no es un edificio ni un expediente. Es un estado de ánimo. Es ese rincón donde las brujas nos reunimos para decir lo que nadie dice, para reírnos de lo serio y darle seriedad a lo que parece una pavada.” En este primer encuentro: - Protocolo de la Hoguera: adiós a los políticos, los alquileres imposibles, los machirulos, los vampiros energéticos y los hombres de Cáncer. Todo lo que sobra… se quema y se transmuta. - Secretaría de Venus en Tanga: astrología y erotismo sin censura. ¿Qué energía nos mueve en esta luna llena de Aries? - Boletín Oficial de Movimientos Planetarios: ChongaZen trae el parte astrológico del cielo y sus efectos terrenales. - Departamento de Estrellas y Sábanas: compatibilidades cósmicas. Hoy: Penélope Cruz y Javier Bardem. - Dirección de Cinematografía Zodiazal: la Dra. Fernanda Garrido recomienda películas según los elementos zodiacales. - Archivos Clasificados de Brujas: homenaje a Violeta Parra, la artista chilena que convirtió su dolor en himno y su rebeldía en legado eterno. Aquí no hay jerarquías ni jefes: mandan las palabras, la energía y la conexión. Si entraste, ya eres parte del aquelarre. En vivo todos los martes a las 20h :(hora España) en YouTube @CanalBarro

programme.title: Hablemos claro de la menopausia con Celia Sancho en Matronas al Rescate.
programme.desc: Bienvenida a Matronas al Rescate, el programa donde se habla claro, se ríe fuerte y se normaliza lo que nadie quiere nombrar. En este episodio, las matronas se enfrentan a un tema que llega antes de lo que crees: la menopausia y la perimenopausia. Para ello, invitan a Celia Sancho, una experta que viene a explicar (sin drama ni eufemismos) qué pasa realmente cuando el cuerpo cambia de guion. ‍️ Gema está enfadada porque no consigue hacer un trámite digital. Leo y Martina se quedan a dormir en el cole. Un paciente chungo, una amiga que no levanta cabeza y un cumpleaños infantil con más puntos en la vagina de la madre que en la tarta. Y entre todo esto: el Día Mundial de la Salud Mental, el parto en casa de Verdeliss, el ADN de tus ex que sigue dentro de ti (microquimerismo) y las cesáreas privadas que duplican lo que recomienda la OMS. Con Celia hablamos de síntomas, soluciones, sexualidad y autoconocimiento, porque no es el fin de nada: es una nueva versión de ti. Conclusión: no es “la edad”, es una nueva temporada hormonal. Y aquí están las matronas para acompañarte con humor, ciencia y cero filtros. Nuevo episodio cada Jueves a las 11h en el canal de YouTube de @CanalBarro Presentan: las Matronas al Rescate.

programme.title: ¿Las pantallas están criando a tus hijos? Sol Macaluso y Fátima de Francisco en Matronas al Rescate
programme.desc: uevo programa de Matronas al Rescate en Canal Barro — y esta vez tocamos uno de los temas más urgentes: cómo las pantallas, las redes sociales y la inteligencia artificial están afectando a la infancia. Las invitadas de lujo fueron: Sol Macaluso, periodista e influencer, que compartió su experiencia personal de crianza en tiempos digitales. Fátima de Francisco, especialista en educación y crianza, que nos habló de los riesgos y efectos reales del uso de pantallas y recomendó libros imprescindibles para madres y padres. Además: Desmontamos trucos virales para dormir bebés, debatimos sobre educación sexual y responsabilidad digital, y Fátima nos dejó helados con un dato impactante: el vídeo pornográfico más descargado de 2017 fue el de “La Manada”, una muestra brutal de la falta de educación sexual y empatía social que seguimos arrastrando. Un programa necesario, incómodo, pero urgente. Matronas al Rescate, todos los jueves a las 11:00 AM (España) en YouTube Canal Barro. #MatronasAlRescate #SolMacaluso #FatimaDeFrancisco #EducacionSexual #Pantallas #CrianzaDigital #CanalBarro #IA #InfanciaDigital

programme.title: Matronas: prematuros, alimentos y un 1,2,3 divertido para explicar los básicos de nutrición
programme.desc: Nuevo jueves en Matronas al Rescate (todos los jueves a las 11:00h en @CanalBarro y venimos cargadas de temas que importan, que ayudan y que, sí, también hacen reír. En este episodio hablamos de: Día Mundial del Prematuro — Atención especializada, UCIN, apoyo emocional y derechos que aún faltan. — La revolución del útero artificial. — Cómo afectan los disruptores endocrinos. Alimentación Complementaria (AC) con Arantxa — Señales reales de que un bebé está listo. — BLW vs cuchara: corte seguro, práctica en directo y cero dramas. — Plato Harvard, cantidades reales y alimentos estrella. — Alimentos NO recomendados antes del año y por qué. — Juegos, fallos, explicaciones y risas. Sueño, hierro, alergias y alimentos clave — Qué favorece el sueño. — Cómo sumar hierro de forma eficaz. — El mapa de alérgenos sin miedo. — Pescados con mercurio: los que sí, los que no. — Todos los nombres del azúcar (sí, TODOS). Seguridad y primeros auxilios — Arcada vs atragantamiento: cómo diferenciarlo de verdad. — Técnica básica que toda madre debería saber. Destete Respetuoso — Qué es, cómo se hace y cómo evitar convertirlo en tragedia griega. — Destete nocturno, diario de tomas y herramientas prácticas. Además: Cumple de Alejandro, fin de semana de caca(s), cocido de mamá, citologías, sección joven con manualidades… y la liada de Ana Brito con la lactancia prolongada. Si eres madre, padre, tía, tío, futura familia o simplemente te obsesiona entender cómo sobreviven los bebés… este episodio te va a salvar media vida. En este episodio de Matronas nos pusimos en modo clásico total: jugamos al mítico “1,2,3… responda otra vez” para explicar los alimentos clave del embarazo sin que nadie cabecee del aburrimiento. Un repaso nutricional hecho juego, con ritmo de concurso vintage y momentos gloriosos que solo pueden ocurrir cuando mezclas conocimiento, velocidad mental y mucha chispa. Además, las matronas bajaron a tierra mitos, explicaron qué comer, qué evitar y por qué, mientras el equipo competía como si hubiera bote final. Es divulgación, sí… pero disfrazada de tele de culto. El próximo episodio promete más ciencia, más humor y alguna que otra sorpresa que hará que estudiar embarazo sea más adictivo que un viernes de gala. #MatronasAlRescate #AlimentaciónComplementaria #BLW #Prematuros #DesteteRespetuoso #Bebés #MaternidadReal #CanalBarro #Emmatrona

programme.title: La carta astral de Pedro Sanchez y Begoña Gómez I Begoña es la que manda I Ministerio de Brujas
programme.desc: Este martes en Ministerio de Brujas (19:00h España, en Canal Barro), las ministras abrieron los portales del poder para leer las cartas astrales de Pedro Sánchez y Begoña Gómez . Lo que descubrieron dejó a todos con la boca abierta: Él, un hombre obsesionado con el poder, encantador pero peligroso en su ingenuidad. Ella, inteligente, estratega y con los pantalones del vínculo. Además, en la Hoguera semanal ardieron los males cotidianos: los Uber que nunca llegan, la gente que mastica con la boca abierta, y un intenso debate sobre identidad y transparencia en las relaciones. La bruja invitada de la semana fue Mercedes Jorqueira, voluntaria de la DANA, que contó en directo su experiencia ayudando en plena catástrofe. En el Departamento de Cinematografía Zodíacal, se recomendaron películas y series de desastres como Chernóbil y Lo imposible. Y en el Archivo de Brujas Quemadas, se honró la figura inmortal de Mercedes Sosa , voz y fuego eterno de América Latina. Ministerio de Brujas — el programa donde el poder se lee en las estrellas, se quema en la hoguera y se transforma en conciencia. programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Nature’s Bounty
programme.desc: In this episode, we start from hiking up volcanoes in Datong. There is a large volcanic cluster with over 30 cones. Then we come to the Hanging Temple – a 1,500-year-old monastery clutching at a cliff of Mount Hengshan. Join us for an adrenaline-pumping adventure!

programme.title: Shenzhen：Before and Beneath the Skyscrapers
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Shenzhen: Past and Present of Shenzhen When it comes to Shenzhen, a pioneering city of China's reform and opening-up, people generally picture it as open, fashionable and bustling. Yet its history and culture are often dismissed as a "cultural desert" or merely a small fishing village. In this episode, we will take you on a journey to gain an in-depth insight into Shenzhen's history and culture.

programme.title: A Canopy of Umbrellas, a Sichuan Serenade
programme.desc: The documentary "A Canopy of Umbrellas, a Sichuan Serenade" follows a father and son as they carry forward the centuries-old craft of making Luzhou oil-paper umbrellas. Each umbrella tells a story—not only of skill, but of family and cultural resilience. As part of CGTN’s original series "Next Stop: China," this episode journeys into the lush bamboo forests of Sichuan, where traditional craftsmanship finds new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Wenzhou
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Wenzhou, southeast China — a city famed for its self-made millionaires. Here he meets the first Chinese shoemaker to expand overseas, and hears the stories of other local entrepreneurs. Along the way, he samples traditional snacks, visits some of China’s oldest lighthouses, and enjoys an evening of Ou Opera. He also learns the craft of papermaking, before heading into the hills to soak in hot springs and wander across ancient covered bridges.

programme.title: The Great Wall Homestay
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, Tianran He's heading to the mountains on Beijing’s northern outskirts, to meet some people his age who have swapped city life for the chance to run guesthouses beside the Great Wall of China.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.6
programme.desc: The mountainous realm of Fujian's centers around the Wuyi range, just opposite Taiwan Province. Join us as we trace a heritage of tea production in ancient villages, marvel at waterside Danxia, and discover terraces where seas of lotuses grow...

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.1
programme.desc: What's not to love about Xishuangbanna? From dazzling night markets to lush bamboo forests, 800-year old tea trees to close encounters with elephants, this tropical city in southwest China has everything, and is where the story of tea begins. Join Foodwise for all the Pu'er tea you can drink and feast on everything from banana flowers to "elephant food"!

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.2
programme.desc: Come get soaked at the Dai people's New Year celebrations! We'll check out buzzing street markets packed with barbecued meats and spicy fruits, crash a foodie auction, and even take part in a rowdy competition, catching fish with our bare hands in the river. All this before hiking through an actual rainforest. We're going to need all the good tea and food we can get!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: Chengde, Where Emperors Escaped to
programme.desc: Chengde is a prefecture-level city in Hebei Province, bordering northeast Beijing and dubbed Beijing’s backyard. Including three parts, this episode features Chengde’s temples, Longhua’s hot springs and Xinglong’s mountains, highlighting the city’s history and abundant natural resources.

programme.title: Shenzhen：When Travel meets Technology
programme.desc: In the second episode of the Shenzhen series, we adopt high-tech aerial shooting and follow the host on a city tour, letting audiences experience Shenzhen’s vigorous development, lush ecological scenery and cutting-edge technological strength.

programme.title: Shared Roots in Wrestling
programme.desc: The documentary “Shared Roots in Wrestling” follows a young wrestler from Tianjin as he journeys to Inner Mongolia to explore the shared heritage of Chinese-style wrestling and Bökh, the region’s national wrestling tradition. Part of CGTN’s original series “Next Stop: China,” this episode uncovers how strength, skill, and resilience connect athletes across city streets and endless grasslands, carrying forward a legacy that transcends geography and generations.

programme.title: Outkirts of Wenzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He explores Wenzhou’s counties. From geological wonders and daring cliffside stunts at the Yandang Mountains, to rafting along the scenic Nanxi River, to harvesting seaweed and shellfish on the mud flats of the Dongtou Islands, Tianran discovers the ingenious ways the people of Wenzhou have transformed the challenges of living between mountains and seas into their greatest strengths.

programme.title: A Village Homestay in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, our presenter Tianran He’s heading out of Beijing proper, to the city’s Miyun District. There he’ll meet some people running guesthouses who gave up their day jobs, in order to achieve the dream of a place of their own in the country.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.7
programme.desc: Jiangsu---an aquatic lowland stitched together by the Yangtze and Grand Canal. From Yellow Sea wetlands populated by red-crowned cranes to the Yangtze estuary's port history, this is a land and coast where maritime legends are made!

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah climb Mount.Huangshan, one of China's most famous mountains, sampling its delicate green tea and the rich flavors of Anhui cuisine, and explore the region's ancient villages and lush bamboo forests featured in the blockbuster film "Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon".

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.2
programme.desc: In Huangshan, Anhui Province, the hosts enjoy a cup of Queen Elizabeth II's favorite tea, as well as the oldest green tea to be exported Europe, and get hands on with quirky local delicacies ranging from "word candy" and tofu made of leaves, to the downright funky flavors of hairy tofu and stinky mandarin fish.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: China Untapped: Suzhou
programme.desc: CGTN’s integrated media cultural and travel program "China Untapped: Suzhou" features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. The show follows a narrative thread of a foreign host touring the city alongside an international business investor. Serving as an explorer and guide, host Alex McCutcheon leads the entire industrial tour across Suzhou. UK businessman Athan Fox, acting as a potential investor and observer, views the city through the lens of commercial inspection and identifies the core strengths and investment potential of Suzhou’s high-end manufacturing sector. The production team traveled across Suzhou’s urban districts, Taicang, Kunshan, Changshu and other areas, visiting over 30 enterprises, research institutions and cultural tourism sites. The program presents a perfect blend of robust industrial strength and the exquisite aesthetics of Jiangnan. The two perspectives complement and validate each other, enabling global audiences to learn about Suzhou’s industrial achievements and unique charm in a way that resonates with their cognitive habits.

programme.title: A Datong You Don't Know
programme.desc: Datong sits in the northernmost part of Shanxi Province, boasting abundant tourist resources and a long-standing history. This episode of our Buddhist cultural journey centers on the Yungang Grottoes. Following the host’s itinerary with the camera, we’ll show you a lesser-known side of Datong.

programme.title: China IRL podcast: Cooler climes and gentle A/C – Surviving the “Dog Days”
programme.desc: On a filming trip in southwest China’s idyllic Dali prefecture, Travelogue hosts Jack Klumpp, Alex McCutcheon and Tianran He share their tricks for cooling down and keeping healthy through the scorching peak of summer. From heading for the hills, to chowing down on a not-too-cold watermelon, they explore ways to harness the power of Mother Nature and achieve inner coolness. Listen in on this impromptu taxi chat for some useful tips on where to go, what to do, and how to beat the heat this summer!

programme.title: 240-Hour Pass in China: Where Pavilions Meet Peaks
programme.desc: Meaning "south of the lake" and "north of the lake," the provinces of Hunan and Hubei in central China take their names from their positions around Dongting Lake – China's second-largest freshwater lake. Nestled along the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, these two provinces are blessed with stunning landscapes and rich local traditions. From the legendary Yellow Crane Tower in Hubei to the breathtaking peaks of Zhangjiajie in Hunan, this journey through central China promises beauty, culture and adventure at every turn. Join CGTN reporter Lucy Lü as she steps into ancient pavilions, uncovers treasured relics, climbs soaring mountains and wanders through riverside towns where tradition and nature come alive in our latest episode of 240-Hour Pass in China: Where Pavilions Meet Peaks!

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.1
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.1
programme.desc: From greening deserts to cleaning up oceans, China is shaping an environmental legacy through individual action, policy coordination, and a circular economy.

programme.title: Bird-eye China Ep.1
programme.desc: Unfolding between the Kunlun, Altai and Tianshan ranges, cradling two vast basins, lies a beautiful land: Xinjiang. Join us on an aerial journey as we ascend the Tianshan to reveal the life-giving secrets of its crystal clear waters, before touching the summit of Bogda Peak, towering 5 km above sea-level, and gliding over the glittering, gem-like Tianchi Lake and the boundless grasslands that extend far beyond what even a bird’s eye can see into the west….

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah climb Mount.Huangshan, one of China's most famous mountains, sampling its delicate green tea and the rich flavors of Anhui cuisine, and explore the region's ancient villages and lush bamboo forests featured in the blockbuster film "Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon".

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.2

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: The hosts are in Fuding, Fujian Province in southeast China for the Dragon Boat Festival, where teams of rowers compete against each other in narrow dragon-shaped boats. From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet!

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night"

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: The Datong Motorcycle Diaries
programme.desc: In this Episode, we explore dragon walls in Datong, the City of Dragon Walls, to create a new tourist trail. The host then rides a motorcycle along Datong’s Great Wall, presenting local culture and scenic spots along the way.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China’s east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life. For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China’s largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess’s birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good fortune. We then learn how silk was manufactured centuries ago, before seeing how imperial‑grade silk is being reinvented for modern‑day fashion.

programme.title: Beijing Unboxed: More Than Palaces
programme.desc: When you think of Beijing, what comes to mind? The Forbidden City, the Summer Palace, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven? These iconic landmarks tell the story of a city with over 3,000 years of history. But Beijing isn't just about the past. It's a vibrant, ever-changing metropolis. Join travel vloggers Lucy and Ioana as they skip the usual tourist spots and show you a side of Beijing where history, modern life, and creativity meet.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.2
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.2
programme.desc: From greening deserts to cleaning up oceans, China is shaping an environmental legacy through individual action, policy coordination, and a circular economy.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.2
programme.desc: Heilongjiang, China's northernmost province, is home to a veritable sea of trees, a forest forged by the Greater and Lesser Khingan Ranges. Beginning our Odyssey at its very northern extremity - a land of snowy Arctic snowscape and dazzling rime-frosts that's a paradise for winter-sports daredevils - we then head for Harbin and its spectacular ice festival in pursuit of some unique snowy adventures...

programme.title: Village Voyage: Before the icon Bruce Lee, there was Shunde in Foshan
programme.desc: Nunchucks. Dark shades. A yellow jumpsuit. That unmistakable nose wipe. Blinding punches and the snake feint – one name says it all: Bruce Lee, the man who brought Chinese martial arts to the world. But every legend has a beginning – and his is less well known. It started in Shunde of Foshan City, south China's Guangdong Province. Join Julian Waghann from the US and Absalom Absalom from Namibia as they trace Lee's roots – following the footsteps of an icon back to where it all began.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei

programme.title: The Datong Motorcycle Diaries
programme.desc: In this Episode, we explore dragon walls in Datong, the City of Dragon Walls, to create a new tourist trail. The host then rides a motorcycle along Datong’s Great Wall, presenting local culture and scenic spots along the way.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China’s east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life. For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China’s largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess’s birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good fortune. We then learn how silk was manufactured centuries ago, before seeing how imperial‑grade silk is being reinvented for modern‑day fashion.

Join Julian Waghann from the US and Absalom Absalom from Namibia as they trace Lee's roots – following the footsteps of an icon back to where it all began.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode Tianran and Hannah are in Hangzhou, a city with over 2000 years of history and capital of two ancient Chinese dynasties. From the famous West Lake to delicate Dragon Well tea, our hosts experience Hangzhou's must-do attractions, savouring the local cuisine and trying everything from winter melon shaped like pork belly, to food cooked according to Traditional Chinese Medicine principles, and even Buddhist noodles and Zen tea.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their tea-tasting journey along Hangzhou's Qiantang River, exploring the region's historical culture and culinary delights. They head to Anding Mountain, enjoying misty tea at the summit. In Longmen Ancient Town, they dive into traditional Chinese clan culture and savor “Sun Quan seitan”. In the gentrified village of Shishe, Hannah falls in love with “gray soup rice dumplings”, while at Qiandao Lake Tianran tries the best fish head and beluga caviar he’s ever had in his life. Their journey ends with a cup of Jiukeng tea and a visit to ancient tea trees.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji’s countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: Nature’s Bounty
programme.desc: In this episode, we start from hiking up volcanoes in Datong. There is a large volcanic cluster with over 30 cones. Then we come to the Hanging Temple – a 1,500-year-old monastery clutching at a cliff of Mount Hengshan. Join us for an adrenaline-pumping adventure!

programme.title: Qingdao: The Jade Island
programme.desc: To boost Qingdao’s international‑oriented publicity and build its profile as an international tourist city, this episode takes us to Qingdao. Through three segments‑‑Modern Qingdao, Historic Qingdao and Internationalized Qingdao, we showcase the diverse facets of this charming city.

programme.title: As Chill as the Pandas in Sichuan
programme.desc: Why are pandas so chill? CGTN's Ioana heads to Sichuan to find out, embarking on a journey that's as bashi (effortlessly satisfying) as it is unforgettable. The documentary "As Chill as the Pandas in Sichuan" invites you to slow down, tune in, and discover what it truly means to live a bashi life.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.3
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.3
programme.desc: From greening deserts to cleaning up oceans, China is shaping an environmental legacy through individual action, policy coordination, and a circular economy.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.3
programme.desc: Hainan- the anchor-point of China's southern frontier, its islands custodians of the vast South China Sea! And perhaps nothing embodies the allure of the oceanic wonderland more than the limpid waters of Sansha. From volcanic northern shores to cutting-edge modern cities, join us on coastal journey dotted with historic lighthouses illuminating a fascinating past and guiding the way to a promising future...

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people’s southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 1
programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. From its Porcelain Tower - one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, to its grand city walls and ancient palaces, join us on a voyage across time to experience the echoes of history in Nanjing's storied bricks.

programme.title: Chengde, Where Emperors Escaped to
programme.desc: Chengde is a prefecture-level city in Hebei Province, bordering northeast Beijing and dubbed Beijing’s backyard. Including three parts, this episode features Chengde’s temples, Longhua’s hot springs and Xinglong’s mountains, highlighting the city’s history and abundant natural resources.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World
programme.desc: When people hear "Spring Festival," they often think of fireworks, red lanterns, and lion dances in the streets. But today, these traditions have grown beyond merely a once-a-year celebration, weaving themselves into people's daily lives across China. The documentary "Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World" embarks on a cultural journey across the nation, tracing how ancient Chinese traditions continue to evolve and engage people worldwide.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.4
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.4
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.1
programme.desc: When Zhejiang's winding river meets the sea it encounters a coastal region studded with islands. On this journey we survey a land of bays, bridges and harbors that is a glorious archipelago of memory, history and culture...

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing
programme.desc: From the local delicacies of Beijing's Ox Street to latest hangouts and contemporary cuisine of the Chinese capital, hosts Tianran He and Eva May will give you a true taste of Beijing, and the fascinating stories and people behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture. In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 2
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the grand old mansions of Nanjing's merchant families and take a stroll through their exquisite gardens, where Nature is incorporated into the architecture. From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 1 - From Relic to Resort
programme.desc: The first episode of the Hotel Series introduces three hotels reconstructed from ancient buildings , each of the hotels has its unique stunning style: 1. Yingui Boutique Hotel reconstructed from ancient buildings with traditional Bai ethnic minority style in Kunming, Yunnan; 2. Imperial Guard Boutique Hotel reconstructed from Anhui Huangshan Huipai architecture; 3. Yellow River Suji Hotel Group in Shapotou, Zhongwei, Ningxia. This episode explores not only their surrounding landscapes, design concepts, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also the distinctive natural scenery and profound local cultural features of each region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art
programme.desc: The documentary "Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art" follows a heritage master and a visionary show director as they carry a thousand-year-old craft into the future. Originating in Liuyang City, Hunan Province, Liuyang fireworks have evolved from ritual folk traditions into a modern art form that integrates cutting-edge technology. Check out how Liuyang fireworks paint stories across the sky.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.5
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.5
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.2
programme.desc: Sichuan's western mountains are a shield safeguarding a true national treasure: the Chengdu Plain, China's very own land of plenty. Join us as we dive from high plateaus into deep gorges, scale snow peaks, and follow rivers in pursuit of an engineering marvel bequeathed by the ancients...

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama – they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

This episode explores not only their surrounding landscapes, design concepts, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also the distinctive natural scenery and profound local cultural features of each region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art
programme.desc: The documentary "Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art" follows a heritage master and a visionary show director as they carry a thousand-year-old craft into the future. Originating in Liuyang City, Hunan Province, Liuyang fireworks have evolved from ritual folk traditions into a modern art form that integrates cutting-edge technology. Check out how Liuyang fireworks paint stories across the sky.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.5
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.5
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.2
programme.desc: Sichuan's western mountains are a shield safeguarding a true national treasure: the Chengdu Plain, China's very own land of plenty. Join us as we dive from high plateaus into deep gorges, scale snow peaks, and follow rivers in pursuit of an engineering marvel bequeathed by the ancients...

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama – they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing
programme.desc: From the local delicacies of Beijing's Ox Street to latest hangouts and contemporary cuisine of the Chinese capital, hosts Tianran He and Eva May will give you a true taste of Beijing, and the fascinating stories and people behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture. In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 2
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the grand old mansions of Nanjing's merchant families and take a stroll through their exquisite gardens, where Nature is incorporated into the architecture. From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 1 - From Relic to Resort
programme.desc: The first episode of the Hotel Series introduces three hotels reconstructed from ancient buildings , each of the hotels has its unique stunning style: 1. Yingui Boutique Hotel reconstructed from ancient buildings with traditional Bai ethnic minority style in Kunming, Yunnan; 2. programme.title: Korela Fortress Museum, Russia
programme.desc: 4K Documentary on Korela Fortress Museum, RussiaAt 160 km from St. Petersburg, there is a small town in northern Russia: Priozersk. Here, on the picturesque banks of the Vuoksa River's mouth and Lake Ladoga, stands the Korela Fortress Museum. Medieval Korela was the most northwestern city of Russia on the Vuoksa River island and served to protect against the Swedes' attack. The foundation date of the Korela Fortress is considered to be 1310. This Fortress is the only surviving Swedish bastion-type Fortress in Russia, on which unique buildings of 6-8 centuries are located: Lars Torstenson's Round Gate Tower, the Old Arsenal, the Powder Magazine, and the Suvorov Arsenal. Initially, the buildings of the Fortress were wooden, but numerous fires destroyed them. Over three centuries, the defensive structure was rebuilt and fortified many times. In the 15th century, Korela occupied an area of 6 thousand square meters, consisted of hundreds of log houses, and its population was more than 300 people. The people of the city were engaged in agriculture and fishing and also professed Christianity.By the sixteenth century, the Fortress acquired the form that has survived to this day. In the eighteenth century, the defense served as a prison for essential state criminals. The round gate tower of Lars Torstenson, located at the junction of the north-west and south-west curtains, is a Swedish building. The time of its construction dates back to 1583-1585. In plan, the tower has an almost circular shape, slightly elongated in the western and eastern directions. During its existence, the Fortress has changed more than one name. ""Korela"" repeatedly passed from Sweden to Russia and back and later belonged to Finland. Each country called this place differently. The original name ""Korela"" came from the name of a tribe that once lived in this area. It's interesting to know that until 19-century Korela was located on an island washed on both sides by the Vuoksa river. Due to its favorable geographic location, the Fortress was practically impregnable.

programme.title: Put your car on TV

Among the competitors are a Lamborghini Aventador and a GMC Chevrolet.

The car with the points wins a stay at the Sofitel Hotel Dubai Jumeirah Beach for two people. Among the presented cars are a limited edition Mercedes SLS and an Audi R8.

programme.title: Put your car on TV

programme.title: Volvo Cars and Epic Games bring real-time photorealistic visualisation
programme.desc:
To offer its customers the best possible user experience, Volvo Cars is bringing photorealistic visualisation technology into its next generation of electric cars through a new collaboration with Epic Games. The companies are teaming up to bring Epic’s Unreal Engine game engine into upcoming Volvo cars, providing unparalleled high-quality graphics inside the cabin.
Epic Games is a leading interactive entertainment and software company probably best known for Fortnite, one of the world’s largest games. Epic Games also develops Unreal Engine, widely considered to be the most advanced real-time 3D creation tool used in various industries beyond games, and which will now be used by Volvo Cars for developing digital interfaces inside its cars and rendering real-time graphics in the car.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

The First Edition offers elegant and timeless design, focusing on maximum comfort and well-being. Other additional features as standard include unique quilted seats, mood lighting, a heated steering wheel, and increased driver’s assistance aids. Attention to detail is clear, from the badging that identifies the car to the jewelled caps on the fuel and oil fillers.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

First Edition badging can be seen to the exterior of the car – a theme that extends inside, with badging on the veneered fascia, as well as embroidery on the seats. Other additional features as standard include unique quilted seats, mood lighting, a heated steering wheel, and increased driver’s assistance aids. Attention to detail is clear, from the badging that identifies the car to the jewelled caps on the fuel and oil fillers.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.
